newsitem.title: BELGIUM: INSTANT VIEW - Tractebel-Electrabel merger plan.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Tractebel-Electrabel merger plan.

text.p: Following are some analyst reactions to a proposal by Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene to merge Belgian utility company Electrabel NV with its parent company Tractebel SA.
Stephane Van Nimmen, Mignon, Hanart Declerck
"Everybody seems to agree on this, the government, the companies and the shareholders, so it looks like it will happen."
"Electrabel shareholders would probably lose some dividend yield, but there could be some form of compensation for them."

"This could be a forerunner for an operation like the merger between Compagnie de Suez and French utility group Lyonnaise des Eaux, whereby (Tractebel parent) Societe Generale de Belgique merges with Tractebel-Electrabel in a daughter-eats-mother operation."
"This could the forerunner to a large restructuring move in the Belgian holding sector."
Danny Wittenberg of broker Dewaay Servais said all the benefits of the merger would be for Tractebel, with little impact on either Electrabel or, depending on the details, its shareholders.
"When Electrabel is absorbed Tractebel will really be considered as a European giant in utility activities and will probably be re-rated," he said.

"It will certainly not be considered any more as a holding company...but it will be considered as a real operational group with a high capital base and increased liquidity. Therefore I see this as especially positive for Tractebel in the long run."

Analyst Guenter Klaffke at Banque Bruxelles Lambert said the direct impact on Electrabel would be minimal, but for Tractebel it would be positive. "The consolidation will contribute a bigger defensive part of earnings (for Tractebel)."

"The effects will be more positive than negative. Of course there will be some dilution, that is clear, but nevertheless the outcome of that will be positive in general as it is giving a more defensive aspect to the group," he added.
